pr.title: feat: disable accounts on report and show new account warning
pr.author: Mythie
pr.head: feat/disable-accounts-on-report

lead: A recipient's report can now disable the sender's account, and signing emails warn when the sender's account is new. Two separate flows, connected by one link.

flows.title: A · A report can disable the sender
B · New-account warning in signing emails

stops.name: reportRecipientRoute
stops.why: A public procedure, no login needed. After recording a report, it now calls disableReportedSender().

note.text: From this line on, one report can end with the sender's account disabled.

checks.does: Any request with a valid recipient token reaches disableReportedSender().
checks.impact: One recipient clicking Report once can disable the sender (Cloud, free plan). The rate limit only stops the same recipient reporting twice within 7 days.
checks.ask: Is one recipient meant to be enough?
checks.alt: organisationMonthlyStat.emailReports already counts reports per organisation. A threshold could build on it.

stops.name: disableReportedSender
stops.why: Loads the envelope owner and plan, asks the rule, disables the user, then queues an email.

note.text: Disabled here. The email is queued later, at line 61, outside this step.

checks.does: disableUser() runs at line 53. The email job is queued at line 61, as a separate step.
checks.impact: If queueing throws, the user stays disabled with no email, and the caller's .catch only logs it.
checks.ask: Is a silent disable acceptable in that case?

stops.name: shouldDisableReportedSender
stops.why: The whole decision to disable: Cloud, free plan, not an admin, not already disabled. Nothing else.

note.text: No account age here. The warning rule (stop 5) does check 48 hours.

checks.does: Returns true for every non-admin, not-yet-disabled user on the free plan in Cloud. Account age isn't checked.
checks.impact: A free account that is years old is disabled by one report, the same as one created an hour ago.
checks.ask: Should disabling be limited to new accounts too?
checks.alt: Reusing NEW_ACCOUNT_PERIOD (sender-trust.ts:8) would make both rules target the same accounts.

stops.name: disableUser
stops.why: Not changed in this PR, but no longer admin-only. A report can now trigger everything below.

note.text: Everything in this transaction can now run without an admin.

checks.does: Disabling expires API tokens and turns off webhooks. enableUser() only sets disabled back to false.
checks.impact: A wrongly reported user who is re-enabled still has expired API tokens and disabled webhooks.
checks.ask: Is losing integrations on a wrong report intended?

stops.name: shouldShowNewAccountWarning
stops.why: Decides who sees the new warning in signing emails: Cloud or opt-in, free plan, user younger than 48 hours.

note.text: Age comes from the sender's user.createdAt.

checks.does: Account age comes from the sender's user.createdAt, not the organisation's.
checks.impact: A new user in an old free organisation triggers the warning. A long-time user who opens a new free organisation doesn't.
checks.ask: Is the sender's personal account age the signal you want?

stops.name: Same decision, three places
stops.why: Each email flow calls the warning rule and excludes self-signers on its own, and the reminder looks at a different user.

note.text: Written differently from the other two, and against envelope.user.

checks.does: send-signing-email and resendDocument check the user who triggered the action. The reminder checks the envelope owner (envelope.user).
checks.impact: For a team envelope sent by someone other than its owner, the invite and the reminder can disagree about showing the warning.
checks.ask: Should all three flows look at the same user?
checks.alt: One helper next to shouldShowNewAccountWarning would keep the three in step.

stops.name: Tests
stops.why: The disable path has end-to-end tests, but CI skips two of them. The warning has no tests at all.

note.text: Skipped unless NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_DOCUMENSO_CLOUD is 'true'. e2e-tests.yml copies .env.example, which doesn't set it.

checks.does: Two of the three new tests skip unless NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_DOCUMENSO_CLOUD is 'true', and CI doesn't set it.
checks.impact: In GitHub CI only the self-hosted test runs. The path that disables accounts isn't exercised.

checks.does: No test renders the warning or calls shouldShowNewAccountWarning.
checks.impact: If a flow stops passing newAccountWarningSenderEmail, every test still passes.
checks.ask: Is that acceptable for a safety warning?

skim.name: send.account.disabled.email
skim.desc: New job. Emails the user and support through the internal mailer, since the organisation's email is blocked once the owner is disabled.

skim.name: AccountDisabledEmailTemplate
skim.desc: Email markup: "Your account has been disabled" plus the support address.

skim.name: Warning in invite and reminder emails
skim.desc: Both templates render TemplateNewAccountWarning when newAccountWarningSenderEmail is set. Its Report sender link opens /report/$token (stop 1).

skim.name: NEXT_PRIVATE_SHOW_NEW_ACCOUNT_EMAIL_WARNING
skim.desc: New opt-in flag for self-hosted. Empty by default.

skim.name: Imports and wiring in the 3 email flows
skim.desc: The parts of send-signing-email, process-signing-reminder and resendDocument not shown in stop 6: imports, createdAt in queries, the template prop.

skim.name: Job registration and one import
skim.desc: jobs/client.ts registers the new job (2 lines), and report-recipient.ts imports disableReportedSender.

skim.name: Rest of report-sender.spec.ts
skim.desc: A reportSender() helper replaces repeated steps, plus the self-hosted and admin tests.

skim.name: disableReportedSender: the query
skim.desc: Lines 1–44: imports and the Prisma query that loads the owner and the plan.

prDescription:
## What
A report from a signing recipient can now disable the sender's account (Documenso Cloud, free plan). Signing, reminder and resend emails warn when the sender's free account is under 48 hours old.

## Read in this order
1. reportRecipientRoute → disableReportedSender → shouldDisableReportedSender → disableUser
2. shouldShowNewAccountWarning, used by send-signing-email, process-signing-reminder, resendDocument

## Behaviour to know
- One report from one recipient is enough to disable a free Cloud account.
- disableUser expires API tokens and disables webhooks; re-enabling doesn't restore them.
- New env var NEXT_PRIVATE_SHOW_NEW_ACCOUNT_EMAIL_WARNING (self-hosted opt-in).

## Tests
3 new e2e tests in report-sender.spec.ts (2 run only with NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_DOCUMENSO_CLOUD=true).
